criteria.criterion: Retrying a retry: A rejected, B ('try again on A') rejected, C asked 'try again on B' gets an Earlier attempt whose request contains A's original request text, and B's findings still appear. New test in crates/athena-cli/tests/lifecycle.rs (or reading.rs unit tests); run `cargo test`.
criteria.evidence: New test retrying_a_retry_carries_the_original_request_redacted builds the A→B→C chain. It asserts that C's brief has '# Earlier attempt', '> try again on <A>', 'original request', '> add a greeting ORIGINAL-CANARY' and the finding text. It passed when I ran it. The test gives A and B the same verdict, so it cannot tell whose findings appear. The code takes findings from B's verification, so this is fine.

criteria.criterion: A single retry (A not itself a retry) yields the same brief as before; existing retry tests pass. Run `cargo test`.
criteria.evidence: original_request returns None when the earlier request is not a retry, so the brief adds no paragraph. The briefs unit test now asserts there is no 'original request' line when the field is None. try_again_on_a_rejected_job_carries_its_request_and_findings_to_the_reader and reader_briefs_carry_an_earlier_attempt_only_when_set both pass.

criteria.criterion: Errors unchanged: unknown job, non-rejected job, and bare 'try again on' are still refused with an error naming the job. Run `cargo test`.
criteria.evidence: try_again_on_a_landed_or_unknown_job_is_refused passes and covers a landed job and an unknown job. The bare 'try again on' case keeps the same bail: retry_reference returns Some(""), which reaches the unchanged bail!. No test covers that case, before or after this change.

criteria.criterion: Everything carried, including the original request, passes through the redactor; a test shows it. `cargo test`, `cargo clippy`, `cargo fmt --check` are clean.
criteria.evidence: The original request is added to texts before redactor.redact_all and is split out afterwards. The new test puts a GitHub-PAT-shaped token in A's request. It asserts the token is absent from the brief and that '[secret:github-pat]' is present, and it passes. Athena's fmt, clippy and test runs passed on this tree.

criteria.criterion: Following the chain cannot loop forever or panic: a visited-id set or depth bound is used, and a code comment says which.
criteria.evidence: original_request keeps a HashSet of visited ids, seeded with the start id, and breaks when insert returns false. Its doc comment reads 'Loop protection: a visited-id set; the walk stops at a job already seen'. It has no unwrap or indexing that could panic: resolve errors and missing records both break out of the loop.

criteria.criterion: CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] records the retry fix. No design doc, review response, or governance file is changed.
criteria.evidence: A '### Fixed' entry was added under [Unreleased]. The diff touches only CHANGELOG.md, lifecycle.rs, briefs.rs and reading.rs.

summary: Pass. The change fixes what the user asked: when you retry a job that was itself a retry, Athena now follows the "try again on <job>" chain back to the first request that was not a retry. A visited-job set stops the walk, so a cycle cannot make it loop forever. The original request is redacted along with everything else carried, and is shown in the new job's "Earlier attempt" section. I ran the new retry-of-retry test, the existing retry tests and the brief unit tests, and all pass. Athena's format, lint and test checks were already clean. All six criteria are met. Two minor findings: (1) the new CHANGELOG "### Fixed" heading accidentally moved the review-1 entry under Fixed instead of Added; (2) no test covers a bare "try again on" with no job named, though that code path is unchanged. As the user asked, answering review 1 was out of scope and was not done.
